quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?

options.text: Severe.
Up to a judge to decide.
Not too harsh.
Optional.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has strict penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to allow for movement.
Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
Use lots of throttle to help you get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet as the helmet could become loose and cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This keeps your motorcycle under control and going in the right direction.

questions.question: Why should group riders avoid pairing up side by side?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Reflections from both helmets may make it difficult for the riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not allow riders the necessary space to maneuver.
It is too difficult for riders on the left side of a pairing to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not allow riders the necessary space to maneuver.
questions.explanation: Do not ride side by side in a group. Neither rider will have enough room to avoid hazards.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: Minimize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Maximize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Maximize your potential for encountering road hazards and allow others to pass you.
Minimize your potential for encountering road hazards and allow you to closely follow another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maximize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you and makes you visible to others. This helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It also gives you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Where is the throttle on a motorcycle?

options.text: Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest
On the left handle grip
On the right handle grip

questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you need to brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.
Apply both brakes.
Not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When you brake, which brakes should you use?

options.text: The front brake only.
The rear brake only.
Both front and rear brakes.
Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while riding?

options.text: Lean as the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.explanation: Sit directly behind the operator and lean when they lean. Sit as far forward as you can without getting in the way, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: If a load is too high, it raises the center of gravity.
If a load is too high, it may interfere with the turn signals.
It may be difficult to see over a load that is placed too high.
Others can't see your load if it is low.

questions.correctAnswerText: If a load is too high, it raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load that is too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can make the motorcycle lose its balance.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. These signs tell you the rules you must follow on the road.

questions.question: Braking in a turn is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straightaway.
More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
Done safely by using the front brake only.
Done safely by using the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes, but you need proper technique and must be very careful.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Not ride during the day.
Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder and stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors when riding so other drivers can see you, even in daylight.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:

options.text: Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.explanation: When turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway, change to a single-file formation. A staggered formation works best on straight roads.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:

options.text: Relax on the handle grips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and let off the throttle. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: To increase your chances of being seen at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Turn your headlight off.
Ride with your headlight on.
Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as closely as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. This is the best way to help other drivers see you at an intersection.

questions.question: When securing a load, you should place the load:

options.text: As high as possible.
As low as possible.
On a sissy bar.
Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Place loads as low as possible. High loads, like those on a sissy bar, raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and hurt its balance. Spread the load evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: If using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not move. Put them toward the back of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign first. Then slowly move forward and stop again just before you reach the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: A jacket that allows the arms to be exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below their ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles with low heels. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of the following is NOT important?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
It fits snugly.
It has no defects.
It looks attractive.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no visible defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar downhill, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?

options.text: It is easier.
It takes longer.
You cannot stop.
It is about the same.

questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which means you need more braking power to stop. Stopping takes longer when riding downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding?

options.text: Always the right side of the lane.
Always the center of the lane.
Always the left side of the lane.
It depends on the road, weather, and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the road, weather, and traffic.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on road conditions, weather, and traffic around you.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Keep a shorter distance from the vehicle ahead.
Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
Ride faster than usual.
Do not use your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark. Slow down and stay farther back from other vehicles at night. Use your high beam when you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: To stop quickly on wet pavement, which brake should you use?

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on wet roads. Apply the front brake slowly to avoid locking up on slippery surfaces.
